note: The test club's statuses and comments for the reseeded season (D313), by competition key (lib/testClub.ts seasonPlan). A status is the card's own player's, at most 140 characters; a comment is anybody's on a card in that competition, at most 280. Ross, 24 Nov 2026: strong language, crude innuendo and nasty banter are fine; graphic sex and slurs are not. Results are never asserted — the cards are made on the day, so a line talks about the round, not the board. Old Tom's and Pierce's remarks are always answered on the same card.

statuses.paddy: Quiet hands, firm lead wrist, finish high and hold it. The finish is everything, boys. Gob, that one's for you. Fuck-all thanks expected.
statuses.jed: Medal play: every shot counts, no gimmes. Which is why I called two of them gimmes. The rules are a living document.
statuses.gob: Greens were rigged. Holes the size of a thimble. I've had bigger things in my mouth. I'm not saying what.
statuses.elaine: Three birdies, a wink at the starter and a man on the 9th who wouldn't stop staring. Best round of my year, honestly.
statuses.pierce: Greenkeeper didn't know who I was. I told him. He still didn't care. Fuck the lot of them, I'm leaving a review.

comments.text: Nobody asked, Paddy. And I'll thank you to keep your shaft talk to yourself.
Gob, you swing like you're being chased out of a brothel. Slow the fuck down, shallow the club and stop trying to impress people who've already left.
The greens weren't rigged, Gob. You were just shit. I love you. Go home.
Mr President, two gimmes on a six-footer in medal play is a felony. I counted them. I'm filing it.
Rules are a living document, he says. Like my last marriage. Constantly amended, mostly in his favour.
Birdies, Elaine? Careful, that's how a woman gets noticed in this club. I'm told I'm quite a catch, if you're ever feeling adventurous.
Pierce, I'd rather get a birdie from a seagull than a compliment from you. Fuck off back to your grievances.
A woman off the medal tees. Next they'll be in the bar after six.
Tom, I outdrove you by thirty yards and I'm cheaper to run. Have a lie-down.
Pierce shot 98. Eighty-two of those strokes were swearing at himself. I counted. Do you want the spreadsheet?
Pierce, you've got the swing of a man trying to get out of a lift full of strangers.
Don, you were flirting with the beverage cart girl on the 14th. She's twenty-two. Her boyfriend has a pitching wedge. Be careful.
Elaine, the beverage cart and I have an understanding. It's the longest relationship I've had that doesn't end in lawyers.

statuses.tom: Seniors' day. Walked it, carried it, hated every bastard step. Pierce took a buggy and a nap. Disgrace to the game.
statuses.pierce: Two-man field. One gentleman, one Tom. I won by being less of a dick than him, which at his age is a tight margin.

comments.text: Tom, that number would get a quiz show cancelled. Maybe it wasn't the buggy. Maybe it's the shit swing.
Pierce, beating one man in a field of two isn't a win. It's a very sad date.
Fun fact: Old Tom Morris won the Open four times. Different Tom. Clearly. Hard watch, that. Hard.
Congratulations, Pierce. You beat a man with two replacement knees and no sense of humour. Frame it, you sad bastard.

statuses.michael: Played behind my brother's ego all day. It was longer than my drive and about as accurate. Not a good day.
statuses.gob: Fourteen lost balls. Not lost: relocated. Trick shot. Magic. Fuck you, Michael, it's magic.
statuses.paddy: Swing felt long and loose. Too loose. Like a hotel mattress. Back to the range with my tail between my legs.
statuses.pierce: Hot day for Pierce Hawthorne. Smooth tempo, big hitter, lovely follow-through. Ladies, you can find me in the bar.
statuses.jed: Played the front nine in the spirit of Eisenhower and the back in the spirit of a man who's been told he can't have a drop.
statuses.sloan: Level with the field, which makes me exactly average. I find that offensive.
statuses.don: Four pints, two birdies, one wedding ring I still haven't found. Good day.

comments.text: Rough day, Mikey? Maybe stick to sitting in an office, pushing paper and being an unbearable prick about it.
Two of those fourteen balls were mine, Gob. You nicked them on the 3rd. I'd like them back. Preferably not from where you've been keeping them.
Paddy, Hogan said the secret is in the dirt. You seem to have found all of it and then swung through it twice.
Jed, your grip is so strong the club's calling a solicitor. Turn it back two knuckles. And stop talking at the top of the backswing, you tit.
Pierce scored well. Statistically even a stopped clock gets the time right. And a monkey with a laptop gets a haiku.
Lovely to see the ladies out on a Saturday. In my day Saturday was for golf and the missus was in the kitchen.
Tom, in your day the shafts were hickory and, I'm told, so was yours. At least the clubs got an upgrade.
Best tempo in the club, Pierce. Shame it all goes to waste on your personality.
Don, a wedding ring in a bunker is the least of your marital hazards.

statuses.jed: President's Prize. A President, prized. A four on the last, after what some would call a lost ball. I call it a spiritual re-tee.
statuses.cj: Spent four hours watching my boss find balls that had demonstrably left the planet. Ask me about the 18th. Actually, don't. I'll scream.
statuses.don: Played well. Drank better. Didn't have to go home until six. Fuck, it's been a good week.
statuses.gob: Trick shot on the 7th tee. Ball's still in the air. Not lost. Merely pending.
statuses.tom: Grand old competition. Spoiled by women in the bar, men in pastel jumpers and some fucking sandwich photographer.
statuses.pierce: Someone dented my Bentley. If it was a golf ball I want it found. Unlike Jed's.
statuses.paddy: Best ball-striking round of my year. Don't tell the putter. We're not speaking.
statuses.michael: Shot a number that'll embarrass my descendants. Kept the ball in the same postcode as the hole. Barely.
statuses.elaine: Played the President's Prize with the President. He explained a rule I've never heard of. I think he made it up on the 12th.
statuses.sloan: Good round. Statistically I'm in the top quartile of players who don't talk to Pierce.

comments.text: Sir, the ball went into the gorse on 18. I watched it go in. The gorse watched it go in. A four isn't destiny, it's a cover-up with a scorecard.
Rule 18.2: a ball is lost after three minutes of search. I searched for two minutes and fifty-eight seconds. Check the footage. And the fucking rule. History will vindicate me.
Jed's drive on 18 went left of left. His four went left of the rules. And the third ball, the one that mysteriously appeared in his pocket, went straight to jail.
The second ball always plays better. Same with wives. Ask me how I know.
What a finish, Jed! Who carries your bag on the 18th — always the same agent, or does the rota change at night? I'd love to thank them personally.
For the record, the ball did come down. In the car park. Through Pierce's sunroof. Gob, it's the best trick you've ever done.
Pierce, it was me. I'm very sorry. I'm not. Send the bill to your wife, she'll want something to read.
Pierce, you drive a Bentley because nobody would ever sleep with you for the personality.
A woman secretary playing in the President's Prize. In my day they couldn't get past the door, never mind the 1st tee.
Tom, I've briefed the world's press through a root canal and a bad divorce. Your opinion is a light fucking breeze.
Great round, Paddy. Honestly the best swing in the club, and I say that with only minor professional jealousy.
Elaine played the President's Prize with the President and didn't once ask for a drop. I'm very impressed. Mostly by the restraint.
Don, I admire a man who drinks his way round. Takes real commitment. I've been doing it for decades, with considerably more success.
Pierce, Don drinks to forget his marriage. You drink because you can't forget yours was a transaction.

statuses.elaine: Ladies' day. No men, no mansplaining, no Pierce. Best four hours of my month. Two Proseccos and a lovely time on the 9th.
statuses.sloan: Long game up on the month. Yes, I keep a spreadsheet. Yes, it has tabs. Yes, one of them is for men who've disappointed me.
statuses.elizabeth: Lovely morning with the girls. So much to talk about! I'm a great listener. Especially when it's about work.
statuses.cj: Played like I brief the press: all words, no follow-through. I need a drink and a man who can keep a secret.

comments.text: Elizabeth, you asked me nine questions about the West Wing floor plan between the 3rd and the 7th. Is everything alright at home?
Only making conversation, CJ! Which door does the President usually use at 7am? Just for my diary.
Ladies' day midweek. Sensible. Keeps the course clear for those of us who actually pay for it.
Tom, the women pay the same subscription, replace more divots, and none of them has ever been banned from the clubhouse bar. I have receipts and a pivot table.
Elaine, if you ever want a man to show you a proper short game, my door's always open. As is my wallet.
Pierce, your door's always open because nobody has ever walked through it. Not even to sell you insurance.
Lovely pace on the putts, Sloan. Now, that left wrist at the top. We need to talk. In private. About your wrist.
CJ's a four handicap in meetings and a twenty-four on the course. I find that deeply comforting.

statuses.tom: Captain's Prize, and the old boy shows them how it's done. Hickory spirit in a steel body. Still got a lovely long swing, thank you.
statuses.jed: The Captain's Prize is named for the Captain, who isn't me. A constitutional oversight I plan to correct. By amendment. Or lobbying.
statuses.gob: Captain asked me not to do the dove thing on the 1st tee again. Did it on the 2nd. I don't take advice well. Or at all. Fuck him.
statuses.paddy: Bad day. Posted my swing video in the group chat for analysis. Nobody replied. I've been dumped by better people than you lot.
statuses.pierce: Played a solid round and was ignored at the prize-giving. I had a speech. A lovely one. About me.
statuses.michael: Kept it in play, kept the peace and kept Gob away from the cutlery. A decent day.
statuses.don: Never raced for the Captain's Prize. Raced for the 19th. Won by a distance.
statuses.sloan: Even par on the back. Told a man his swing looked like a seizure. He thanked me. Men are strange.

comments.text: Decent card, Tom. My model says the last time you posted one like that, Truman was in office.
Sir, you have no jurisdiction over the club constitution. You have a 3 handicap on parole and the self-control of a toddler near a biscuit tin.
The dove is fine, everyone. The captain is not. Sorry, captain. Gob, your dick-measuring contest with the starter is over.
Paddy, I'd analyse your swing, but you'd take it as an insult. Like I do. Fucking hell, I understand you now.
Watched the video, Paddy. Your hips fire before your shoulders, like a man who doesn't want to hang about. Also you filmed it vertically, which is a war crime.
Michael, a word to the wise: you'll never get anywhere in this club by being reasonable. Take it from a man who's been unreasonable his whole life.
Thanks, Pierce. Noted, and ignored. You're also the least reasonable man I've ever shared a car park with.
Don, you strike me as a man who keeps secrets. Do you happen to know anyone in government? Anyone at all? I'm only asking out of curiosity.
Elizabeth, I know everyone in advertising and half the fucking bartenders in Manhattan. If you want state secrets, ask a barman.
Pierce, the speech was about you. We all got that from the first line. The rest was just a lot of breathing.
Sloan, a woman with a swing like that should stick to marketing.
Pierce, I'm a financial journalist who shot even par. Please stick to whatever it is you do. Is it standing near things?

statuses.elaine: Played with Jed and CJ. Jed explained the Rules of Golf to me eleven times. I've gone home. Birdied the 14th. Left him on the 15th.
statuses.don: Went round in the time it takes some men to find their ball. Then a Scotch. Then another. Then a lovely woman asked if I was alone.
statuses.pierce: Medal play is a test of character. I passed. The scorecard did not. Fuck the scorecard.
statuses.michael: Kept it in play. Kept the family out of it. A good day.
statuses.cj: Bad day. The President won't stop quoting the Rules. I want to put a seven-iron somewhere the sun doesn't shine. Back soon.
statuses.jed: A medal round of great integrity. I have the receipts. Mostly.
statuses.gob: Birdie on the 12th. Did it with my eyes shut. Don't ask me how. I don't know. Neither did the ball.

comments.text: Elaine, in 1744 the Gentlemen Golfers of Leith wrote thirteen rules. Thirteen! I have memorised all thirteen and invented four more.
And all four of yours are about you getting a gimme, Jed. You absolute bellend.
Tough round today, CJ! Are you sleeping? Late nights in the Situation Room? How late, roughly? Which nights?
Elizabeth, that's the fourth week running you've asked. I've started a file. On you.
Pierce, you have the character of a man with a chequebook. Medal play wants a man with a putter.
The scorecard has a character too, Pierce. It's a crime scene. There are bodies. Mostly yours.
Gob, you're swaying off the ball like a man in a tight corridor. Stay centred. Turn, don't slide. I'm not saying it's a euphemism but it is.
I sway because the crowd moves me, Paddy. Something you wouldn't know. Have you ever met a crowd? Shite.
Don, how are you always so calm out there?
Because I'm not out there, Michael. I'm in the bar in my head. And she's very, very understanding.

statuses.cj: Points. Lots of them. If the President would like to discuss, he can make an appointment through my office. After I've had a drink.
statuses.gob: Retiring from golf. Back next Saturday. Fuck golf. Fuck the haters. See you at 8.
statuses.tom: Old Tom still has it. Where 'it' is the only working knee left in this group. Shot my age. In yards. Over three days.
statuses.paddy: Lost my swing. If found, please return. Answers to 'one plane'. Reward: a fuck of a lot of range balls.
statuses.michael: Poor round. Good company. Gob said fuck eleven times on the 4th alone. Personal best.
statuses.pierce: Not my best. But the day Pierce Hawthorne loses is the day the world ends. And it's not that day.
statuses.sloan: Hit 14 greens, three-putted six of them. Statistically that's not my fault. Statistically it's the greenkeeper's.
statuses.elaine: Decent round. Ignored three men on the course. Pierce, take the hint, it's a Titleist.
statuses.don: Nobody told me there'd be golf. I thought it was a drinks reception. Same fucking result.
statuses.jed: A round of immense dignity, spoiled only by the Rules of Golf, my own caddie and the wind. Particularly the wind.

comments.text: CJ, an outstanding round. No President has ever been prouder of his staff.
Sir, please be proud quietly. There's a pool reporter in the bar and you've got that look again.
He retires every week. Next Saturday he'll come back billed as 'the comeback'. With pyrotechnics.
Retiring is the first thing he's done all day with any conviction.
Paddy lost his swing. I've been asked to find it. And, ta-da, it's in the clubhouse. With the other lost causes.
Good round, Tom. Funny how well it goes the week you don't complain about the ladies' tees.
I complained, Sloan. Quietly. Like a gentleman.
Quietly, Tom. On a public feed. With your name on it. And a photo.
Pierce, you shot a number. That's all I can say without a lawyer present.
Congratulations CJ! Shall we celebrate? Your place? Bring your work laptop, I'd love to see what you're working on!
Sloan, you three-putted six greens and I still want to buy you a drink. Statistically that's flattering.
Elaine, Pierce followed you round the 9th. I saw it. As a matter of conscience, I'd like it on the record.
Don, you're not at a drinks reception. You've been at the 19th since the 6th.
